question: What is the best everyday advice a nurse can give to help prevent chronic constipation?

options.A: Take a strong saline purgative every morning before breakfast
options.B: Reduce all fluid intake to allow stools to form more slowly
options.C: Avoid eating local foods like beans and green vegetables
options.D: Increase intake of water, dietary fiber, and physical activity

explanation: Simple and natural is best! Drinking water, eating fiber, and staying active keep the digestive tract happy and regular. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T2#GNS223_U3_T2_h8)

question: Which compress is best for a patient who twisted their ankle just ten minutes ago?

options.A: Alternating hot and steaming compress
options.B: Room-temperature dry wrap
options.C: Cold compress
options.D: Warm compress

explanation: For fresh injuries (acute injuries), cold therapy is your best friend to keep swelling and pain down. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T9#GNS221_U3_T9_h2)

question: What is the biggest benefit of a psychologically safe work culture on the ward?

options.A: Employees never experience any form of physical fatigue or tiredness.
options.B: Patients are discharged from the hospital twice as fast.
options.C: Hospital operating costs are reduced to absolute zero immediately.
options.D: Staff feel comfortable reporting near-misses without fear of harsh punishment.

explanation: When people aren't terrified of being yelled at, they will speak up about close calls or mistakes. That open communication is what keeps patients truly safe! [learn more](GST321_U3_T4#GST321_U3_T4_h4)

question: Which human sense is widely believed to be the absolute last to fade before a patient dies?

options.A: Hearing
options.B: Touch
options.C: Sight
options.D: Taste

explanation: Hearing usually stays intact longer than other senses. That's why we always encourage families to keep talking and comforting their loved ones right up until the end. Beautiful nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS221_U4_T4#GNS221_U4_T4_h4)

question: A nurse manager notices that gloves and syringes are being wasted carelessly on the ward. What nursing responsibility does this touch on?

options.A: Conducting large epidemiological research surveys
options.B: Setting national health insurance laws
options.C: Resource stewardship and controlling costs
options.D: Diagnosing rare genetic disorders

explanation: You're doing great! Resource stewardship simply means taking good care of hospital supplies so there's always enough equipment left to treat patients safely without wasteful spending. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h6)

question: A patient is breathing rapidly at 34 breaths per minute and straining their neck muscles to breathe. What should you do right away?

options.A: Document the findings as normal vital signs for an adult and schedule a routine follow-up
options.B: Recognize this as severe respiratory distress and prepare immediate oxygen and triage support
options.C: Advise the patient to lie flat on their back and sleep off the exhaustion
options.D: Administer an oral antipyretic medication for presumed fever

explanation: Using accessory neck muscles and breathing super fast are clear SOS signs of severe breathing trouble. Time to act fast with oxygen! [learn more](GNS321_U2_T13#GNS321_U2_T13_h2)

question: Even after physical withdrawal fades, why is quitting smoking still so tough?

options.A: Commercial cigarettes contain permanent cellular dyes
options.B: Social laws make it illegal to stop smoking abruptly
options.C: The body continues producing natural nicotine forever
options.D: Psychological habits and environmental triggers remain deeply ingrained

explanation: The mental habit and social triggers stick around long after the physical chemicals leave the body. Don't worry if this takes time to master! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h4)

question: What does the acronym IEC stand for in public health?

options.A: Investigation, Environment, and Community
options.B: Immunization, Education, and Care
options.C: Information, Education, and Communication
options.D: Infection, Evaluation, and Control

explanation: IEC is a core public health strategy that stands for Information, Education, and Communication, used to guide community health promotion. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h1)

question: What exactly is salpingitis?

options.A: Bacterial colonization of the outer vulva
options.B: Malignant growth inside the uterine muscle wall
options.C: Fungal overgrowth within the vaginal vault
options.D: Infection and inflammation of the fallopian tubes

explanation: Salpingitis simply means inflammation in the fallopian tubes, usually caused by bacteria moving up from the lower reproductive tract. You've got this! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT strictly needed for normal blood flow to body tissues?

options.A: A healthy and effective cardiac pump
options.B: Sufficient circulating blood volume
options.C: Normal functioning of the liver and spleen
options.D: An intact and open blood vessel network

explanation: While your liver and spleen do amazing filter work, the absolute basics needed for body perfusion are just a pump (the heart), pipes (blood vessels), and fluid volume! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T5#GNS123_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which hospital expense usually goes up as more patients are admitted?

options.A: Annual administrative software licenses
options.B: Facility property insurance premiums
options.C: Monthly building mortgage payments
options.D: Disposable syringes and IV tubing

explanation: Medical supplies are variable costs. More patients mean you use more supplies, so the total price goes up. [learn more](GST322_U2_T1#GST322_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which type of nerve fibers send those sharp, instant pain signals?

options.A: Ruffini fibers
options.B: Merkel fibers
options.C: C fibers
options.D: A-delta fibers

explanation: Brilliant! A-delta fibers are wrapped in myelin, which lets them rush electrical impulses quickly to cause that sharp first pain. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T5#GNS211_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why should you tell a patient to avoid clearing their throat aggressively right after a laryngoscopy?

options.A: It prevents the doctor from writing the final discharge summary.
options.B: It increases the patient's blood pressure and heart rate significantly.
options.C: It forces the residual topical spray down into the stomach too fast.
options.D: It can cause trauma or irritation to the recently numbed vocal cords.

explanation: Spot on! Since the vocal cords are still a bit sleepy and vulnerable, harsh throat clearing can easily bruise or injure them. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T4#GNS221_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the standard safe temperature for storing most routine vaccines in a fridge?

options.A: 30°C to 40°C
options.C: 2°C to 8°C
options.D: 15°C to 25°C

explanation: Always remember this golden rule for vaccines: keep them chilled between 2°C and 8°C so they stay potent and safe to use. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T4#GNS125_U4_T4_h3)

question: What is the safest way to open the steam tent when the treatment is done?

options.A: Rip open the plastic tent quickly to let fresh air rush in
options.B: Leave the steam running while taking the patient out
options.C: Turn off the generator and open the canopy gradually
options.D: Wait until the room temperature drops below normal

explanation: Opening it slowly prevents a sudden blast of cool air from chilling your damp patient. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T8#GNS212_U2_T8_h7)

question: Which psychosocial issue is closely linked to a weaker immune system in seniors?

options.A: Active community engagement
options.B: Social isolation
options.C: High daily fluid intake
options.D: Regular physical exercise

explanation: Humans need connection! Loneliness and social isolation don't just hurt the heart emotionally—they can actually wear down physical health and immunity in older adults. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T5#GNS321_U3_T5_h8)

question: Why is observing chest symmetry important during the breathing assessment?

options.A: It tells the nurse if the patient has a chronic respiratory infection
options.B: It determines whether the patient has eaten recently
options.C: It helps detect uneven lung expansion caused by injury or trapped air
options.D: It is the only way to calculate the exact respiratory rate accurately

explanation: Asymmetrical chest movement often points to serious problems like a pneumothorax, flail chest, or hemothorax requiring immediate intervention. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T8#GNS112_U7_T8_h4)

question: Why are daily reviews of invasive lines and breathing tubes an important part of complication prevention?

options.A: Hospital insurance policies require equipment to be changed daily.
options.B: It gives the nursing staff less paperwork to complete at shift change.
options.C: Removing them as soon as they are no longer needed lowers infection risks.
options.D: Patients prefer to have new lines poked into them every morning.

explanation: Every day a tube or line stays inside the body gives bacteria more time to enter and cause a severe infection. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is another common name for therapeutic dietary counselling?

options.A: Holistic wellness education
options.B: Preventive lifestyle coaching
options.C: Medical nutrition therapy
options.D: General community wellness

explanation: Therapeutic counselling uses specific food and nutrient adjustments to treat active illnesses, which is known as medical nutrition therapy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h4)

question: Why does the body's immune system attack mismatched blood?

options.A: It tries to repair the damaged cells using white blood cells
options.B: It recognizes the foreign antigens as nonself and makes antibodies
options.C: It runs out of normal plasma proteins to handle the extra fluid
options.D: It mistakes the red blood cells for harmful bacteria

explanation: You've got this! The immune system's main job is spotting foreign invaders. When it sees unfamiliar antigens on donated red blood cells, it treats them as dangerous and attacks. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which extrapyramidal side effect looks and acts almost identical to natural Parkinson's disease?

options.A: Pseudoparkinsonism
options.B: Tardive dyskinesia
options.C: Acute dystonia
options.D: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome

explanation: 'Pseudo' means fake! Pseudoparkinsonism gives patients tremors, muscle stiffness, and a shuffling walk that looks just like Parkinson's, but it's actually caused by the medication. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T6#GNS223_U6_T6_h6)

question: Which hormone acts like a natural relaxant to keep the uterus calm during pregnancy?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Progesterone

explanation: Progesterone is the uterus's best friend—it keeps everything calm and relaxed until it's time to meet the baby. Keep up the fantastic work! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h3)

question: A patient in skeletal traction suddenly complains of severe pain and numb toes in the affected leg. What should you do first?

options.A: Check the equipment alignment and notify the physician immediately
options.B: Increase the hanging weight to relieve pressure
options.C: Give a sleeping pill and turn the patient on their side
options.D: Remove the skeletal traction pin at the bedside

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Sudden pain and numbness mean blood flow or nerves might be squeezed. Always check the setup first and call the doctor right away. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T9#GNS221_U1_T9_h3)

question: Why do oxygen cylinders and wall outlets always need strict 'No Smoking' safety signs nearby?

options.A: Oxygen strongly supports combustion and makes fires spread rapidly
options.B: Tobacco smoke clogs the small holes in the nasal cannula prongs
options.C: Smoking interferes with the machine's internal electrical circuits
options.D: The smell of smoke ruins the purity of the medical gas supply

explanation: Oxygen itself doesn't burn, but it feeds fires aggressively. Even a tiny spark can turn into a massive flame in seconds around supplemental oxygen! [learn more](GNS212_U2_T9#GNS212_U2_T9_h7)

question: A new mum is worried about being very forgetful two weeks after giving birth. What should you do?

options.A: Refer her immediately for a complex magnetic resonance imaging scan of the brain
options.B: Notify the primary physician that she is showing signs of early-onset dementia
options.C: Instruct her to stop breastfeeding immediately to restore normal vitamin levels
options.D: Reassure her that temporary cognitive shifts and memory lapses are normal adaptive changes

explanation: Be her comfort! Postpartum 'brain fog' is totally normal as the brain adjusts. Reassuring her goes a long way in easing her anxiety. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T6#GNS121_U7_T6_h6)

question: Which common organism causes most vaginal and urinary tract fungal infections?

options.A: Escherichia coli
options.B: Trichomonas vaginalis
options.C: Candida species
options.D: Neisseria gonorrhoeae

explanation: Candida species (like Candida albicans) are the usual suspects behind yeast infections in our private parts. You've got this! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T3#GNS223_U8_T3_h1)

question: What do we call a non-living object—like a stethoscope, door handle, or bed sheet—that can pass germs from one person to another?

options.A: Reservoir
options.B: Vector
options.C: Carrier
options.D: Fomite

explanation: You've got this! Non-living items that carry germs around are called fomites. Think of things like dirty linens or blood pressure cuffs moving microbes from patient to patient. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h1)

question: Where does Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) rank when we talk about safety controls?

options.A: As the last line of defense
options.B: As a complete hazard eliminator
options.C: As the most effective method
options.D: As an engineering intervention

explanation: Gloves, masks, and aprons are crucial, but they are our final backup when other safety measures like equipment design or policies aren't enough on their own. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T7#GNS225_U7_T7_h4)

question: How do water-soluble vitamins behave differently from fat-soluble vitamins in the body?

options.A: Water-soluble vitamins can be stored in the liver in large toxic amounts
options.B: Fat-soluble vitamins play no role in normal human physiological processes
options.C: Water-soluble vitamins are excreted in urine and require more frequent intake
options.D: Fat-soluble vitamins cannot be absorbed without adequate daily hydration

explanation: You're doing great! Water-soluble vitamins dissolve in body fluids, meaning any extra gets peed out. That's why we need a fresh supply of them regularly in our meals. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h3)

question: What is the best way for a nurse administrator to handle a valid complaint about poor hospital services?

options.A: Punish the patient for speaking out against the hospital management
options.B: Investigate the complaint fairly and put measures in place to fix the issue
options.C: Ignore the complaint completely so the issue disappears on its own
options.D: Blame junior nursing staff in public without checking the facts

explanation: Handling complaints openly builds trust! Investigating fairly helps fix underlying problems and shows patients that their voices matter. [learn more](GST321_U10_T3#GST321_U10_T3_h7)

question: Which nursing action directly helps prevent deep vein thrombosis in a patient on bedrest?

options.A: Encouraging early ambulation and leg exercises
options.B: Massaging the calf muscles firmly to break up small clots
options.C: Applying warm heating pads directly over the fracture site
options.D: Keeping the injured limb elevated above heart level all day

explanation: Movement is medicine! When muscles contract, they act like a pump pushing blood back to the heart, stopping it from pooling and forming clots. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T23#GNS222_U1_T23_h9)

question: How long does the postpartum puerperium period typically last?

options.A: Three months
options.B: Nine months
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: Two weeks

explanation: You've got this! The puerperium lasts for about six weeks after childbirth. This is the special time the mother's body needs for her reproductive organs to gently return to their normal, non-pregnant state. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h1)

question: Your patient on a nasal cannula complains of a dry, sore throat and a mild nosebleed. What is your best nursing action?

options.A: Increase the oxygen flow rate to flush the nasal passages
options.B: Recommend adding humidification to the oxygen setup as prescribed
options.C: Remove the oxygen permanently and document refusal of care
options.D: Switch the patient to a tight-fitting non-rebreather mask

explanation: Dry medical gas can be tough on delicate mucous membranes. Adding moisture (humidification) is the perfect fix to soothe that dryness and irritation. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T9#GNS212_U2_T9_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a right that patients keep while on psychiatric parole?

options.A: The right to completely ignore court-ordered treatment without consequences
options.B: The right to give informed consent for general healthcare
options.C: The right to access legal help and representation
options.D: The right to be treated with dignity and professional respect

explanation: You nailed it! Parole comes with conditions—ignoring your treatment plan means breaking those conditions, which leads back to clinical or legal intervention. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T8#GNS314_U5_T8_h6)

question: Why is running low on folate (folic acid) especially risky in early pregnancy?

options.A: It impairs rapid cell division and increases the risk of neural tube defects
options.B: It stops the placenta from attaching to the uterine wall entirely
options.C: It causes immediate destruction of all maternal white blood cells
options.D: It directly causes sudden maternal hemorrhage during the first month

explanation: Folate is a builder's best friend for DNA and fast-multiplying cells! Without enough in early pregnancy, the baby's brain and spinal cord (neural tube) can fail to develop properly. That's why routine folic acid is a must. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T020#GNS226_U2_T020_h3)

question: What is a major long-term risk for patients dealing with ongoing autoimmune inflammation and immunosuppression?

options.A: Increased risk of cardiovascular disease and infections
options.B: Complete regeneration of destroyed organ tissue
options.C: Permanent stabilization of normal blood pressure
options.D: Total immunity against all forms of cancer

explanation: Constant inflammation wears down blood vessels over time, and medicines that lower immunity leave patients more open to infections. [learn more](GST114_U4_T8#GST114_U4_T8_h8)

question: When checking a patient's standing posture from behind, what is the first thing a nurse should look for?

options.A: Symmetry of the shoulders and hips
options.B: The strength of the hand grip
options.C: The speed of the patient's heart rate
options.D: The exact color of the patient's eyes

explanation: By checking if both shoulders and hips line up evenly, you can quickly spot early signs of spinal curves like scoliosis. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T5#GNS112_U4_T5_h6)

question: At 28 weeks, an ultrasound shows a slight thickening of the mother's left heart ventricle. What does this mean?

options.A: It is a normal physiological response to increased cardiac workload
options.B: It indicates long-standing chronic hypertension
options.C: It points to an acute myocardial infarction
options.D: It shows early signs of congenital heart failure

explanation: Exactly! The heart muscle works harder during pregnancy, so it thickens just a little bit to handle the extra load safely. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T2#GNS121_U7_T2_h3)

question: What is the main danger if the uterine lining is exposed to constant estrogen without enough progesterone to trigger shedding?

options.A: Rapid thinning and complete wasting of the muscle layer
options.B: Sudden development of ovarian cysts on both sides
options.C: Increased risk of endometrial hyperplasia and cancer
options.D: Permanent closure of the cervix

explanation: Without regular periods to clear it out, the uterine lining can overgrow (hyperplasia) from too much unopposed estrogen, which increases cancer risks over time. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h6)

question: At what centimeter of cervical dilation does the plotting of the active phase on a standard partograph typically begin?

options.A: 10 centimeters
options.B: 4 centimeters
options.C: 7 centimeters
options.D: 1 centimeter

explanation: The active phase and routine partograph plotting traditionally commence once the cervix reaches 4 centimeters of dilation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h5)

question: Which action must a nurse take BEFORE giving a high-risk medication?

options.A: Ask the patient to sign a waiver releasing the hospital from liability
options.B: Gather baseline clinical data and relevant lab values
options.C: Discontinue all other medications the patient is currently taking
options.D: Double the prescribed dose to test for allergic reactions

explanation: Baseline checks give you a reference point to compare against if the patient develops adverse symptoms later. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h6)

question: What happens in your body during the normal urination reflex?

options.A: The ureters close tightly to push extra fluid backward.
options.B: The transitional epithelium absorbs all the leftover fluid.
options.C: The detrusor muscle contracts and the internal sphincter relaxes.
options.D: The detrusor muscle relaxes and both sphincters tighten.

explanation: Spot on! Urination is a team effort: the bladder wall squeezes (detrusor contracts) while the doorway opens up (internal sphincter relaxes). [learn more](GNS121_U2_T3#GNS121_U2_T3_h5)

question: A nurse wants to know if child stunting rates decreased two years after starting a food program. What action is this?

options.A: Evaluating long-term program impact
options.B: Conducting a 24-hour dietary recall
options.C: Monitoring daily vitamin distribution
options.D: Screening a child with MUAC tape

explanation: Checking rates after a long period to see if the main goal was achieved is a classic evaluation of impact. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T003#GNS227_U3_T003_h8)

question: Why do healthcare workers need to do an N95 fit test every year?

options.A: Weight changes or dental work can change how the mask seals
options.B: Manufacturers change their plastic formulas yearly
options.C: Hospital rules just want to renew licenses
options.D: Filters expire chemically after one year

explanation: Our faces change over time! A fit test ensures your mask still seals safely against your unique face shape. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h5)

question: Why is assessing transport availability crucial before approving a home delivery?

options.A: To ensure a quick transfer if an obstetric emergency arises
options.B: So the nurse can catch a ride back to the clinic
options.C: To transport traditional birth attendants to the venue
options.D: To bring extra furniture into the room

explanation: Delays in reaching a hospital during an unexpected emergency can cost the lives of both mother and baby. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h6)

question: What is the name of the slippery mass of food formed in the mouth before swallowing?

options.A: Micelle
options.B: Feces
options.C: Chyme
options.D: A bolus

explanation: The tongue and saliva combine chewed food and mucus into a rounded mass called a bolus for easy swallowing. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why does chronic kidney disease often lead to secondary hyperparathyroidism?

options.A: Urine output drops so low that calcium crystallizes inside the bladder.
options.B: Failing kidneys cannot activate vitamin D or clear phosphate properly.
options.C: The kidneys start producing parathyroid hormone in place of the glands.
options.D: Renal failure directly destroys all four parathyroid glands within weeks.

explanation: When kidneys fail, they struggle to clear phosphate and activate vitamin D, which drops your calcium levels and forces the parathyroid glands to work overtime. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T11#GNS222_U2_T11_h3)

question: When should public health nurses begin control measures during a suspected disease outbreak?

options.A: Only when international health agencies give direct written permission
options.B: As soon as strong clinical evidence suggests an outbreak, without waiting for every lab result
options.C: Only after writing a final research paper for an academic journal
options.D: After all affected patients have been completely discharged from the hospital

explanation: Exactly! In public health, speed saves lives. Waiting for every single lab result can cause preventable harm. Great clinical instinct! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h6)

question: Why must a nurse evaluate the road conditions and distance to the hospital for a home birth?

options.A: To calculate how much fuel the nurse's car will burn
options.B: To find the cheapest taxi fare for the family
options.C: To decide if the baby will be born during the day or night
options.D: To plan a safe and fast emergency transfer if complications happen

explanation: If labor goes wrong, bad roads or long distances can delay life-saving hospital care. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h6)

question: Which of the following is an essential component of primary health care?

options.A: Building private pharmaceutical manufacturing plants in every town
options.B: Providing free luxury health insurance for political leaders
options.C: Performing complex open-heart surgery in rural clinics
options.D: Immunization against major infectious childhood diseases

explanation: Maternal and child health services, including routine immunizations, form a core component of essential primary health care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a good reason to be careful with the Kubler-Ross model?

options.A: It guarantees every patient will have a completely painless death
options.B: Treating the stages as strict rules can hurt individualized care
options.C: It might miss cultural differences in how people grieve
options.D: Patients often skip or repeat stages

explanation: Spot on! The model maps out emotions—it has nothing to do with curing physical pain or guaranteeing a pain-free passing. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T3#GNS221_U4_T3_h7)

question: Which chemical messenger in the brain gets flooded when someone takes addictive substances?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Histamine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: Dopamine is the brain's 'feel-good' chemical. Addictive drugs hijack this natural reward pathway, making the user crave more. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T11#GNS125_U2_T11_h4)

question: What is a major health limitation shared by all traditional and natural family planning methods?

options.A: They do not protect against sexually transmitted infections
options.B: They require daily surgical wound dressing changes
options.C: They cause permanent blockage of the fallopian tubes
options.D: They increase blood pressure above normal levels

explanation: Because traditional methods don't use physical barriers like condoms or chemical germ-killers, they leave users fully exposed to STIs. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T009#GNS226_U6_T009_h7)

question: A nurse manager creates a strict handwashing policy to prevent infections, relying on standard operating procedures. Which theory is primarily applied here?

options.A: Bureaucratic management theory
options.B: Human relations management theory
options.C: Pure contingency management
options.D: Quantitative management science

explanation: Establishing formal rules, standard operating procedures, and safety regulations reflects bureaucratic theory. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is a thyroid storm?

options.A: A sudden drop in thyroid hormone levels causing deep sleep
options.B: A harmless swelling of the thyroid gland during cold weather
options.C: An infection of the outer neck tissue near the windpipe
options.D: A life-threatening emergency marked by extreme fever and high heart rate

explanation: A thyroid storm is a dangerous complication of severe hyperthyroidism where all body systems speed up to a critical, fatal level if untreated. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T7#GNS211_U1_T7_h7)

question: What is the main goal of teaching pregnant mothers about good nutrition during antenatal care?

options.A: To help the mother lose weight during the first trimester
options.B: To guarantee a completely painless labor and delivery
options.C: To eliminate the need for routine blood pressure checks
options.D: To prevent low birth weight and support fetal development

explanation: You've got this! Proper nutrition is key to helping the baby grow strong and healthy while keeping the mother in great shape throughout her pregnancy. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T011#GNS227_U7_T011_h1)

question: How does vitamin C from fruits help your body use iron better?

options.A: It breaks down complex proteins in animal meat
options.B: It directly converts red blood cells into hemoglobin
options.C: It prevents the liver from storing excess iron
options.D: It enhances the absorption of non-heme iron in the gut

explanation: You got it! Vitamin C teams up with plant-based iron in your tummy, making it much easier for your body to absorb. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T010#GNS227_U4_T010_h1)

question: A community nurse notices many residents with severe watery diarrhea who all use the same stream. What is the best immediate step?

options.A: Advise residents to stop washing their hands after using the toilet
options.B: Report the cluster and investigate the water source as a potential reservoir
options.C: Prescribe broad-spectrum antibiotics to every healthy person in town
options.D: Close down the local hospital to prevent airborne contamination

explanation: When people sharing a water source get sick together, checking that water supply is a classic nursing move to find the culprit! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T80#GNS214_U1_T80_h5)

question: Why should a nurse check local market days and religious schedules before setting a date for a community health talk?

options.A: To comply with international trade and economic regulations
options.B: To avoid scheduling conflicts that would prevent people from attending
options.C: To make sure the weather is always cool and rainy
options.D: To ensure the nurse can buy fresh food items after the meeting

explanation: You nailed it! Checking local routines ensures you pick a time when people are actually free to show up and learn. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T1#GNS214_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of adding a small 'sustainability mark-up' to DRF drugs?

options.A: To pay the personal salaries of the hospital medical director
options.B: To protect the fund against inflation, wastage, and future stock depletion

question: Which potential risk is primarily associated with repeated or multiple CT scan procedures?

question: Which local Nigerian vegetable is commonly used in soups to provide essential iron and vitamins for nursing mothers?

question: When a nurse visits a family's home to care for an infant, why is it helpful to view yourself as a 'guest'?

question: Which of these is a great example of secondary data in a community assessment?

question: What structures divide the internal nasal cavity into left and right halves?

question: What happens when alveolar macrophages try to swallow heavy loads of mineral dust?

question: A new mother looks exhausted and tells you she feels totally hopeless weeks after delivery. What should you do first?

question: Public health officers visit local clinics and review registers directly to find hidden cases during a cholera outbreak. What type of surveillance is this?

options.A: Syndromic surveillance

question: If a research study is 'verifiable,' what does that mean for other nurses?

options.C: Other researchers can replicate it and get similar results
options.D: The results change every time a new nurse looks at them

question: Why has the demand for formal geriatric homes been on the rise lately?

options.A: Urbanization and changing family structures
options.B: Older adults universally preferring institutional living
options.C: Government bans on caring for elderly relatives at home
options.D: The complete disappearance of traditional family values

explanation: As cities grow and more family members move away for work, formal residential care becomes necessary to support our elders. Great job thinking it through! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T13#GNS324_U5_T13_h1)

question: Which of these is a normal, expected reaction shortly after getting a shot?

options.C: Mild soreness and swelling at the injection site
options.D: Widespread blistering rash across the entire body

question: Where should you cough or sneeze if you don't have a tissue nearby?

options.A: Into your inner elbow or upper sleeve

options.C: Directly into the palm of your bare hand
options.D: Into the air away from other people

question: What is the main goal of the science of improvement in healthcare?

options.A: Reducing hospital operational costs by cutting nursing staff numbers
options.B: Punishing staff members who make medication administration errors
options.C: Discovering entirely new medical treatments through laboratory trials
options.D: Applying proven knowledge to reliably improve daily care processes

question: What is an effective way for a nurse to start talking about loss with a patient?

options.C: Reminding them of all the other blessings in their life

question: What is the main job of progesterone during the female reproductive cycle?

options.C: Stimulating the growth of breast milk ducts at birth
options.D: Lowering female body temperature during menstruation

question: Why do economists look at health spending as a percentage of GNP rather than just raw cash amounts?

options.A: It stops inflation from happening in local community pharmacies
options.B: It calculates the exact salary every registered nurse should earn
options.C: It allows fair comparison between countries with different economic sizes and populations
options.D: It predicts the exact number of disease outbreaks in a year

explanation: Using percentages helps us fairly compare health spending between big economies and smaller nations without getting confused by different currency values. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h2)

question: How should you respond when a client uses unhealthy coping tricks like total denial or locking themselves away from others?

options.A: Immediately discharge the client from home care services
options.B: Ignore the behavior because it will naturally resolve itself
options.C: Confront the behaviors with empathy rather than harsh judgment
options.D: Scold the client for failing to follow the rehabilitation plan

explanation: Harshness pushes people further into their shell. Meeting them with patience and understanding gives them a safe space to start healing emotionally. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T2#GNS324_U2_T2_h4)

question: A patient is finding it hard to follow a strict diet and exercise plan. What should the team do?

options.A: Double the medication dose without telling the patient
options.B: Re-evaluate the plan with the patient to fit their actual lifestyle
options.C: Discharge the patient from community care for non-compliance
options.D: Report the patient to local law enforcement authorities

explanation: Exactly! If a plan isn't working, we adjust it together with the patient so it fits their real life and is easy to follow. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h5)

question: A patient stands up, closes their eyes, and immediately starts swaying heavily and losing balance. How do we document this?

options.A: Positive Romberg test
options.B: Positive Brudzinski sign
options.C: Presence of resting tremor
options.D: Normal cerebellar function

explanation: That's a positive Romberg test! It happens when a patient can stand fine with their eyes open (using vision to balance), but loses it when they close their eyes. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T20#GNS222_U3_T20_h6)

question: Which shift scheduling practice best helps reduce fatigue-related nursing errors?

options.A: Implementing sensible roster planning with protected rest periods
options.B: Eliminating handovers entirely to keep nurses at the bedside
options.C: Allowing back-to-back double shifts without mandatory breaks
options.D: Requiring all junior staff to work consecutive night shifts indefinitely

explanation: Correct! Well-designed rosters and actual time to rest give the brain a chance to recover, keeping both you and your patients safe. [learn more](GST319_U5_T7#GST319_U5_T7_h4)

question: What is the very first step a nurse must take to become truly culturally competent?

options.A: Insist that patients adopt modern hospital habits

options.C: Examine their own personal biases and values
options.D: Memorize the medical laws of every country

explanation: Self-reflection is key! Before we can understand others, we have to look inward and recognize our own unique cultural viewpoints and biases. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h5)

question: What is a key action public health nurses take to improve community nutrition?

options.A: Growing all the crops needed for the entire country inside hospitals

options.C: Passing strict laws to ban all processed foods globally
options.D: Taking over the management of international cargo shipping lines

explanation: Spot on! Nurses play a huge role by checking nutritional status and teaching families how to cook healthy, pocket-friendly local meals. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T030#GNS227_U2_T030_h8)

question: Which Nigerian food item is an excellent local source of both plant protein and healthy fats?

question: What is the main benefit of regularly assessing immunization programs in primary health centers?

question: Which of these phrases should a nurse avoid saying to a grieving family member?

options.A: "Everything happens for a reason."

options.C: "I am here for you if you want to talk."
options.D: "It is okay to cry and feel sad right now."

question: Which machine uses high-pressure steam to sterilize infectious items?

options.A: Autoclaving
options.B: Incineration

options.D: Chemical burial

question: How does Rifampicin stop TB bacteria from multiplying?

question: What immediate nursing care is standard practice right after the baby is born to prevent heavy bleeding?

question: What is a very common trigger for dangerous autonomic dysreflexia in a patient with a spinal cord injury?

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

question: How is terminal (palliative) sedation different from physician-assisted suicide?

question: An AED has just been brought to the side of an adult patient in cardiac arrest. What is the very first thing the nurse should do with it?

question: What is the main goal of musculoskeletal rehabilitation?

question: When is the right time for a nurse-midwife to practice hand hygiene in the labor ward?

question: Why should a nurse avoid performing blind finger sweeps when clearing an airway obstruction?

question: When is it best for a nurse researcher to choose a qualitative study design?

question: How does naloxone work so quickly to reverse an opioid overdose?

question: Which statement about depression in older adults is FALSE?

question: What is a core goal of immunization within Primary Health Care?

question: What must a nurse do before changing how they care for patients based on a new research paper?

question: How often should you check the baby's heartbeat during the second stage of normal labour?

question: What physical sign is tested by tapping the facial nerve near the cheek to check for low calcium?

question: What happens when a patient takes two different medications that both depress the central nervous system?

question: What is the primary function of a hormone receptor on a target cell?

question: Why is a host so important in the disease transmission cycle?

question: Which of these is NOT a typical limitation of questionnaire-based studies?

question: A couple already has a healthy 5-year-old child, but has been trying for 3 years to have another baby without success. What do we call this?

question: How do antibodies cause too much hormone to be released in conditions like Graves' disease?

question: What is the main difference between a spontaneous abortion and an induced abortion?

question: A healthy pregnant woman at 26 weeks gestation goes for her routine antenatal clinic. Why is a glucose screening typically included?

options.A: To check for gestational diabetes that can develop during pregnancy
options.B: To confirm the exact gestational age of the growing fetus
options.C: To test her kidney function against pregnancy hormones
options.D: To measure how much iron she is storing in her liver

explanation: Pregnancy hormones can cause insulin resistance, making routine screening for gestational diabetes essential during the second trimester. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h3)

question: What is the main job of capillaries in our blood circulation?

options.A: Allowing oxygen and food nutrients to pass into body tissues
options.B: Pushing blood forward with rhythmic squeezes
options.C: Storing extra blood when we are resting
options.D: Pumping blood back to the heart under high pressure

explanation: Capillaries have very tiny, thin walls that act like a marketplace, letting oxygen and nutrients pass from the blood into your body cells while taking away waste. You've got this! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T11#GNS213_U1_T11_h1)

question: Why might you need to watch a patient for whole-body (systemic) effects after applying a topical cream or patch?

options.A: Skin application always causes widespread allergic reactions.
options.B: Topical drugs change the local skin temperature, affecting blood pressure.
options.C: Some topical agents are designed to cross the skin barrier and enter the bloodstream.
options.D: All topical drugs automatically travel to the liver first before working.

explanation: Spot on! While many stay local, formulations like transdermal patches are specially made to pass through the skin into the bloodstream to heal the whole body. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T12#GNS215_U6_T12_h1)

question: You are managing a patient with acute PPH. Which of these actions is completely WRONG and dangerous?

options.A: Checking vital signs every 5 to 15 minutes
options.B: Instructing the patient to walk around to encourage drainage
options.C: Calling for help from the multidisciplinary team right away
options.D: Setting up large-bore IV lines for fluid replacement

explanation: Never let a bleeding, shock-prone patient walk around! That can instantly cause her blood pressure to bottom out and lead to a collapse. Strict bed rest is a must. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T012#GNS226_U4_T012_h6)

question: What is a very common cause of esophageal strictures (narrowing) that need dilation?

options.A: Chronic acid reflux disease
options.B: Benign gastric hypersecretion
options.C: Excessive dietary fiber intake
options.D: Congenital throat widening

explanation: When stomach acid keeps splashing up into the esophagus over a long time, it irritates the tissue, causes scarring, and makes the passage narrow. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T19#GNS212_U1_T19_h3)

question: What is the recommended chest compression rate per minute for an adult in cardiac arrest?

options.A: 140 to 160 compressions per minute
options.B: 100 to 120 compressions per minute
options.C: 60 to 80 compressions per minute
options.D: 40 to 60 compressions per minute

explanation: A rate of 100 to 120 per minute mimics a normal working heart rate to push blood forward effectively. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T4#GNS315_U4_T4_h2)

question: A nurse sits down with local leaders and clinic staff to resolve a disagreement over immunization times. Which role is this nurse playing?

options.A: Patient
options.B: Prosecutor
options.C: Auditor
options.D: Mediator

explanation: You nailed it! A mediator steps in between two opposing sides to help them talk it out and find a peaceful, workable solution. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h3)

question: What is the most important infection control habit for a nurse to teach a patient on immunosuppressive drugs?

options.A: Stopping all physical exercise completely
options.B: Wearing heavy winter clothing outside at all times
options.C: Drinking only distilled water
options.D: Doing thorough and frequent hand hygiene

explanation: Never underestimate the power of clean hands! Proper hand hygiene is your patient's number one defense against picking up harmful germs in everyday life. [learn more](GST114_U4_T7#GST114_U4_T7_h7)

question: During which phase of cancer development do cells gain aggressive traits and learn to spread?

options.A: Progression
options.B: Initiation
options.C: Promotion
options.D: Encapsulation

explanation: Progression is the final, full-speed-ahead phase where the cells become truly malignant and start invading. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T7#GNS321_U1_T7_h4)

question: Why should a nurse apply gentle pressure to the nasolacrimal duct after giving eye drops?

options.A: To help spread the liquid evenly across the eyeball surface
options.B: To stop the patient from blinking too rapidly
options.C: To seal the eyelids shut until the medication dries completely
options.D: To keep the medication from draining into the nasal passage and causing systemic effects

explanation: Blocking the tear duct stops the medicine from entering the nose and bloodstream, keeping its action localized to the eye. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T10#GNS122_U1_T10_h5)

question: Which animal is well-known as the natural reservoir host for transmitting Lassa fever in West Africa?

options.A: Mastomys rat
options.B: Anopheles mosquito
options.C: Domestic livestock
options.D: Migratory birds

explanation: The multimammate rat (Mastomys) carries the Lassa virus and sheds it in homes through its urine and droppings. Good public health detail to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h4)
